clue.text: Fellow is certain to crack

parts.note: taken as written
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A man who is sure he can crack a problem or a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a narrow split or cleft, a synonym for a crack in rock or ice.

clue.text: Terror, after the last of these is removed from cargo

indicators.note: the clue works backwards: once the letter is taken out of the cargo word, the terror word remains, so we put that letter in

parts.note: fright means terror

indicators.note: the final letter of the word these is the one picked

explanation.surface: A fear left over once some goods are unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: This is worded in reverse: 'is removed from' says the terror word is what the cargo word leaves once E (the last of 'these') goes, so E is put into FRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by ship, train or lorry, which is what cargo means.

clue.text: Step out over smouldering coal, then fall

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above, that is before, the next
out signals that the letters of step are put out of their order

parts.note: an ember is a piece of smouldering coal

explanation.surface: Someone walks on hot coals and then trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the first word, and 'over' puts it above the coal in this down entry. 'Fall' is the American word for autumn, not a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: September is the first month of autumn, which Americans call fall.

clue.text: Disturbance caused by superior clique

parts.note: up means higher or superior in position
a set is a clique or exclusive group

explanation.surface: An upheaval caused by a snobbish in-crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disruption or disturbance, as in a stomach upset or a political upset.

clue.text: Run and see conversion, to make certain

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so the letters of run and see are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby player runs, then watches the conversion kick to seal the win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversion' suggests a rugby kick after a try but is the anagram signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to guarantee or confirm it happens.

clue.text: Gives points, for musical range

definitions.meaning: a navigator's ... shows the points north, south, east and west
the ... of a voice or instrument is the span of notes it can reach

explanation.definitionFit: One instrument shows directions; the same word names the full span of notes a singer can manage.

clue.text: Indifference to bird-song on lake and headland

parts.note: coo is the soft call of a dove or pigeon
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off the birdsong over a lake and cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolness is a lack of warmth or enthusiasm, an aloof indifference.

clue.text: Young lady for the most part philanthropic, shows apprehension

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: miss is a young unmarried woman
giving means generous or philanthropic

explanation.surface: A generous young woman is nervous about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension about what may happen.

clue.text: In Capri, luxuriate for a few weeks

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is tucked inside the run of words Capri, luxuriate

explanation.surface: Enjoying a short holiday lounging on the island of Capri.
explanation.definitionFit: The month in question lasts thirty days, roughly four weeks.

clue.text: Having second thoughts about nasty sneer at poet

indicators.note: about here signals the letters for second thoughts are turned round

parts.note: PS, a postscript, adds afterthoughts to a letter

indicators.note: nasty suggests something mangled, so the letters of sneer are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having sneered at a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PS into SP; 'nasty' rearranges SNEER into ENSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan writer of The Faerie Queene, a poem in praise of Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Reveals the old attitudes

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
poses are attitudes or postures struck for effect

explanation.surface: Showing that the old ways of thinking are on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to uncover or lay it bare.

clue.text: Extraordinarily verbose remark

indicators.note: extraordinarily means out of the usual pattern, so the letters of verbose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that goes on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe can mean to comment or say, a synonym of remark.

clue.text: Sell a green rat — it comes from these islands

indicators.note: comes from suggests the letters of the phrase are worked into something new, an anagram

explanation.surface: A pet shop trying to sell a green rat imported from the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes from' rearranges all of SELL A GREEN RAT IT, so the pronoun is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba, Hispaniola, Jamaica and Puerto Rico make up this larger group of Caribbean islands.

clue.text: Also, impounding luggage in the Caribbean

indicators.note: impounding means seizing and holding, so one word holds the other

parts.note: too means also
a bag is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: Customs in the Caribbean also hold on to someone's luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: The island is the smaller half of Trinidad and Tobago, in the southern Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Gooey casserole I slung out

indicators.note: to casserole is to stew things together, so the letters of the phrase are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a sticky stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casserole' is a verb here, the anagram signal on I SLUNG OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutinous means sticky like glue, which is what gooey describes.

clue.text: Transferring property, the fool ignores mid-west removal

definitions.note: the clue phrase describes the role, a person who hands over property

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: removal means the letters named are taken out of the word ignores
mid points to the middle letters of the word west

explanation.surface: An idiot overlooks the midwest when moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-west' looks like the American region, but it asks for the middle two letters of the word west, removed from ignores.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the assignor is the party who transfers a right or property to another, the assignee.

clue.text: Blink, seeing object caught in turn-up, at art exhibition

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: it is the object in a sentence like 'see it'
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone blinks on seeing something odd in a trouser turn-up at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' reverses IT + C + IN to give NICTI. The Tate is the group of national art galleries in London, Liverpool and St Ives.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictitate is the formal word for to wink or blink.

clue.text: Didn't like being ordered to go, in a rush

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a rush, a tall marsh plant
sent means dispatched or ordered to go

explanation.surface: Someone sent off in a hurry was upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' is the marsh plant, not a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter about it, to dislike it.

clue.text: Motorist going round Inner Circle with jolly celebrator

indicators.note: going round means the motorist encircles the next piece

parts.note: a car user is a motorist
a circle is drawn as the ring shape O

explanation.surface: A driver on the Inner Circle road in Regent's Park meets a party-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner Circle is a ring road in Regent's Park, London; here it simply supplies a ring shape, held inside the motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks and makes merry, a reveller.

clue.text: High favour?

parts.note: a favour is a ribbon or rosette worn as a badge, and this one is worn high up on a hat

explanation.definitionFit: A cockade is a rosette or knot of ribbons pinned to a hat as a badge.

clue.text: Supporter of cooked breakfast

parts.note: the supporter is a little holder for a boiled breakfast item, not a fan of fry-ups

explanation.definitionFit: This small cup holds a boiled egg upright at the table.

clue.text: Allowed to have fish starter, then toasted teacake

indicators.note: starter means the fish piece comes first, before the word for allowed

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone may have fish as a first course and then a toasted cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A pikelet is a thin British crumpet, a griddle cake eaten toasted with butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a regional British crumpet, served toasted at teatime.

clue.text: Vehicle's faulty bearings caused shocks

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a vehicle is a car, and the 's adds an S
E and S, east and south, are compass bearings

explanation.surface: A car's worn bearings gave its driver some frights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges CARS + ES; 'bearings' sounds mechanical but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Scares are sudden frights or shocks.

clue.text: Eccentric kind of engineering produces this racket

indicators.note: engineering means building or rearranging, so the letters of the phrase are reworked

explanation.surface: An odd branch of engineering leads to a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineering' is the anagram signal on all of ECCENTRIC KIND OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a swindle, and this trick wins a victim's trust in order to cheat them.

clue.text: Lady of the manor

indicators.note: of here means made of, so the lady is formed of the letters of the word manor

explanation.surface: The woman who owns the country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The lady is made 'of the' MANOR: its five letters rearranged give her name, Norma, as in Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's name, famously the title heroine of Bellini's opera.

clue.text: Scattered stack of nails

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters of stack are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pile of nails spilt across the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacks are short sharp nails with broad heads.

clue.text: The distinctive quality left behind, departing from it?

indicators.note: behind means the word for left comes after

parts.note: an air is a distinctive quality or manner, as in an air of mystery
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a certain character behind as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not departed but the sailors' left, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers depart from this place by plane.

clue.text: Here in the North Atlantic finding fabulous bird, key to everything?

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of myth and fable
K is used as an abbreviation for key
all means everything

explanation.surface: Finding a legendary bird in the ocean, the answer to all things.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockall is a tiny rocky islet west of Scotland, familiar to British listeners of the shipping forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: The islet stands alone in the North Atlantic, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Pleased, after treatment, to have passed on

indicators.note: after treatment means the letters of pleased have been worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone happy after medical care has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed on' suggests death, but here it means time that has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by or moved on.

clue.text: It's questionable for group to imprison us on the quiet

indicators.note: to imprison means one piece encloses the others

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
taken as written
P, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: A dubious cult secretly locks people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is doubtful and open to question.
